lines.text: Abram says a servant, Eliezer of Damascus, will be his heir, but the LORD says his own son will be.
The LORD tells Abram to count the sand, and Abram believes Him, and it is credited as righteousness.
The LORD reminds Abram He brought him out of Ur, and Abram splits animals but drives birds of prey away.
While Abram sleeps, the LORD says his descendants will be enslaved four hundred years in a land not their own.
A smoking firepot and flaming torch pass between the halves, and the LORD gives land from Egypt to the Jordan.
